html:
A statement of faith issued by the eastern emperor Zeno in 482, drafted by Acacius, bishop of Constantinople. Its name means "act of union". It tried to reconcile Christians who accepted the Council of Chalcedon with those, strong in Egypt and Syria, who rejected it.

It condemned both Nestorius and Eutyches and avoided the disputed words "one nature" and "two natures". It said nothing in favour of Chalcedon's definition. Zeno hoped this would keep Egypt and Syria loyal without offending others.

It pleased few people. Strict opponents of Chalcedon found it too weak. Pope Felix III saw it as a betrayal of Chalcedon and in 484 excommunicated Acacius, starting the Acacian schism between Rome and Constantinople. It lasted until 519, when the emperor Justin I dropped the Henotikon and made peace with Rome. The split with the non-Chalcedonian churches remained.
